blocks.etymology: The noun is from Middle English secret, from Latin sēcrētum. Doublet of secretum. Displaced Old English dēagolnes (“a secret”). The verb is from the noun.

senses.definition: something that is kept unknown from others or shared with very few people

examples.en: Can you keep a secret?
examples.vi: Bạn có thể giữ bí mật được không?

examples.en: They made the decision in secret.
examples.vi: Họ đã đưa ra quyết định trong bí mật.

senses.definition: the best or only effective method to achieve or understand something

examples.en: Hard work is the secret of his success.
examples.vi: Chăm chỉ là bí quyết dẫn tới thành công của anh ấy.

senses.definition: a fact or phenomenon about something that people do not yet understand

examples.en: Scientists are trying to uncover the secrets of the ocean.

wiktionary.gloss: A piece of knowledge that is hidden and intended to be kept hidden.

blocks.etymology: The figurative act of throwing a gift (senses 1 and 2), prize (sense 3) or merely an object (sense 4) in someone's face.

examples: I tried to make up after the argument, but he just threw it in my face and stormed off.
wiktionary.gloss: To reject some act in a spiteful manner.

examples: I supported you for months, and you've just thrown all that in my face by losing your job.
wiktionary.gloss: To repay an act of kindness with disappointment or betrayal.

examples: Bringing the kids along was clearly just an excuse to throw it in my face after the divorce.
wiktionary.gloss: To lord over someone by exerting dominance, following a successful confrontation; sometimes in a subtle or snide manner.

examples: She always throws that time I cheated in my face when we argue. It was ten years ago!
wiktionary.gloss: To raise a past transgression in order to admonish someone.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see throw, something, in, someone, face.
